title: Sonu @ Amar v. State of Haryana

content.caseIdentity: Sonu @ Amar v. State of Haryana, (2017) 8 SCC 570
content.facts: The appellant was convicted of kidnapping for ransom and murder largely on Call Detail Records (CDRs) which had been exhibited during trial without any defense objection regarding the absence of a Section 65B certificate.
questionsBeforeCourt: Whether an objection regarding the lack of a Section 65B [BSA s. 63] certificate can be raised for the first time before the appellate court.
content.ratioDecidendi: An objection that an electronic record is not accompanied by a Section 65B certificate relates to the "mode of proof" and procedural admissibility, not inherent inadmissibility. Objections to mode of proof must be raised at the time of marking the document as an exhibit in the trial court; if omitted, the objection is deemed waived and cannot be raised for the first time in appeal.
content.holding: Conviction upheld; appellate objection regarding absence of certificate rejected as barred by omission to object during trial.
content.relevance: Crucial tactical trial authority: warns defense counsel that failure to raise a contemporaneous Section 63 objection during exhibit marking forfeits the point in appeal.
